card: Prevents unauthorized cross-origin RPC execution by rejecting any HTTP request carrying an Origin header with HTTP 403 Forbidden before authentication checks occur. When users log into Bitcoin Core RPC via a web browser, cached credentials can be leveraged by other web pages to execute local RPC calls without permission, even if the browser blocks reading the response. The author points to existing tools like Block Clock that document direct browser-to-RPC connectivity. This unconditionally blocks all requests sending an Origin header, which will break reverse proxies and browser extensions that attach this header unless they adapt.
changed_since_previous: No changes to the approach or code; the diff and functional test implementation are now attached.
evidence: PR description links to third-party tools documenting direct browser RPC connectivity (such as Block Clock) and earlier discussion in #12040 demonstrating browser-based transaction broadcasting.
problem: When users connect to Bitcoin Core RPC through a web browser, the browser caches HTTP authentication credentials for the host and port. Malicious web pages visited in the same browser can issue cross-origin requests to the RPC endpoint; although the same-origin policy blocks the page from reading the response, state-changing RPC commands still execute on the node using the cached credentials.

risk.why: Legitimate API clients, web integrations, or reverse proxies that forward or inject an Origin header will be rejected with HTTP 403.

summary: Rejects incoming JSON-RPC HTTP requests that include an Origin header before evaluating authentication. This stops web browsers from submitting cross-origin RPC requests that execute using cached HTTP credentials.
